clue.text: Time will be on its side

definitions.text: Time will be on its side

parts.words: Time will be on its side
parts.note: a tall building with a dial on its face, so the hours are literally displayed on its side, playing on the phrase 'time is on my side'

explanation.definitionFit: A tower bearing a clock face shows the time on its walls, which is the literal reading of the idiom.

clue.text: Stagger up and get a dirty look

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for stagger is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to stagger is to reel

explanation.surface: Someone lurches to their feet and is met with a nasty glance.
explanation.definitionFit: A leer is an unpleasant, suggestive sidelong glance, so a dirty look describes it.

clue.text: Use a knife to draw blood from the rib

parts.note: to use a knife is to cut
to let blood is the old surgical phrase for drawing it

explanation.surface: A surgeon slices into a patient to bleed them from the ribcage.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlet is a chop of meat, often taken from the rib section of lamb or veal.

clue.text: Such lights are on all day

definitions.text: Such lights are on all day

parts.words: Such lights are on all day
parts.note: signals at road junctions run round the clock, unlike lamps that come on only at night

explanation.definitionFit: Signals controlling vehicles at junctions are named after the vehicles that use the road.

clue.text: The load, we hear, must take its turn

indicators.note: this tells us the word is spoken, so a word with the same sound is entered

parts.note: a load is a weight

explanation.surface: A heavy burden must queue patiently before being dealt with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must' is a link word; to wait is to hold back until one's turn comes.
explanation.definitionFit: To wait is to stay until one's own opportunity arrives in a queue.

clue.text: Worn by those shortening sails?

parts.note: sailors who take in sail by tying reef points wear close-fitting double-breasted jackets of the same name as themselves

explanation.definitionFit: A reefer jacket is a sailor's short thick coat, and one who reefs sails is also called this.

clue.text: Don't join in the play reading?

definitions.text: Don't join in the play reading?

parts.words: Don't join in the play reading?
parts.note: abstaining from an activity is expressed by an idiom that also suggests having no role when actors read a script

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to abstain, and here also hints at an actor without a role in a reading.

clue.text: Yet such ads are seen by the public

definitions.text: Yet such ads are seen by the public

parts.words: Yet such ads are seen by the public
parts.note: small newspaper advertisements share a name with documents kept secret, which is the paradox of the 'yet'

explanation.definitionFit: Small-print newspaper ads are grouped by type, and that word also means officially secret.

clue.text: Trip lasting some months in the US

definitions.meaning: to trip is to stumble, a tumble
Americans call autumn by this name

explanation.definitionFit: A trip is a stumble or tumble, and Americans name autumn this way.

clue.text: Take to heart?

parts.note: read literally, moving things into the middle or core, rather than being moved emotionally

explanation.definitionFit: To bring administration into a single core or middle is literally taking it to the heart.

clue.text: Heated complaints

parts.note: not angry grumbles but illnesses involving high body temperature

explanation.definitionFit: These illnesses raise body temperature, so they are literally heated ailments.

clue.text: Bridge expert

parts.note: not a card player but the officer in command on a ship's bridge

explanation.definitionFit: A ship's commanding officer works from the bridge and is the master of it.

clue.text: End of soldiering in Asia for military force

indicators.note: the final letter of soldiering is placed inside the word for Asia

parts.note: Asia is a continent

indicators.note: the last letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A soldier's posting finishes in Asia, where an army is stationed.
explanation.definitionFit: A contingent is a group of troops contributed to a larger force.

clue.text: It may provide music to Pinafore production

indicators.note: the letters of to Pinafore are produced in a new arrangement, playing on staging the operetta

explanation.surface: A piano accompanies a staging of the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta HMS Pinafore.
explanation.walkthrough: HMS Pinafore is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera; 'production' suggests staging it but signals rearranging TOPINAFORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano is a keyboard instrument that supplies music.

clue.text: Where a saint still has some standing

definitions.text: Where a saint still has some standing

parts.words: Where a saint still has some standing
parts.note: a statue of a holy figure stands motionless in a recess in a church wall

explanation.definitionFit: A recess in a wall holds a statue, often of a saint, standing still.

clue.text: On tour, I look round capital

parts.note: a tour is a trip

indicators.note: the short word for look is turned round

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: A traveller on a sightseeing trip gazes around a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is a link word. TRIPOLI is the capital of Libya.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital city of Libya.

clue.text: Way part of a match turns into matches

indicators.note: both pieces together are turned around and read backwards

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
a set is part of a tennis match

explanation.surface: Part of a sporting fixture changes direction, becoming a series of games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses STSET to give TESTS; 'into' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Test matches are international cricket matches, called tests for short.

clue.text: Names objects of especial interest, say

indicators.note: this signals that the word is spoken and a same-sounding word is entered

parts.note: sights are the attractions tourists go to see

explanation.surface: Someone lists the things that particularly interest them.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite is to mention or quote by name, so names as a verb fits.

clue.text: Ham was presumably served at his table

definitions.text: Ham was presumably served at his table

parts.words: Ham was presumably served at his table
parts.note: Ham is a son of the biblical ark-builder, so he would have sat at his father's table, not been the meat

explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the ark-builder's sons were Shem, Ham and Japheth.

clue.text: Transport army team

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force
XI is eleven, a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: Vehicles are moving an army squad.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi is a hired car, a means of transport.

clue.text: Reports it's very warm on board

indicators.note: being on the board means sitting within the letters for a ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the board one goes on
very warm means hot

explanation.surface: News comes in that the weather is sweltering on the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' is a link word; reports here are bangs of gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunshot makes a report, a loud bang, so shots are reports.

clue.text: Wrested apart and scattered

indicators.note: wrested apart means the letters are pulled into a new order

explanation.surface: Something was torn away and its pieces flung everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To strew is to scatter, so strewed is scattered.

clue.text: Kind of gamble is without point

parts.note: a spec is a speculation, a gamble

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the word is wraps the point

parts.note: E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: A certain type of bet is said to be pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: A species is a kind or sort.

clue.text: Cut off, making one extremely behind schedule

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
so means very, extremely
being behind schedule is being late

explanation.surface: Someone running very late is stranded alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate is to cut off from others.

clue.text: Seen to have a rash

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both noticed and marked with spots like a rash.

clue.text: Distressing twitch about to irritate

indicators.note: the twitch goes round the word for irritate

parts.note: a tic is a nervous twitch
to rag is to tease or irritate

explanation.surface: A nervous twitch that keeps annoying is upsetting.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic events are deeply distressing.

clue.text: He was an honest feller!

parts.note: the legend of the first US president who chopped a cherry tree and could not tell a lie, so an honest fellow and an honest feller of trees

explanation.definitionFit: The cherry-tree legend says the young future president confessed to chopping the tree.

clue.text: He employs American with hesitation

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: An employer is an American who hesitates.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is one who employs or makes use of something.

clue.text: Harbour a spy

definitions.meaning: a breakwater or pier enclosing a harbour
an agent planted inside an organisation

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a harbour breakwater and a planted secret agent.

clue.text: See 24
One on the staff backs school

indicators.note: the school name is read backwards

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A teacher on the staff supports the school.
explanation.definitionFit: A note is written on a musical staff (stave).

clue.text: Private matter that never comes to light

definitions.text: Private matter that never comes to light

parts.words: Private matter that never comes to light
parts.note: something hidden and shameful kept from discovery, with a hint that it stays in shadow

explanation.definitionFit: A shameful secret kept hidden is never brought into the open.
